papers.full_text: Abstract Background The increasing incidence of dengue in Europe, combined with the spread of invasive mosquito species, raises concerns about the emergence of new vectors. Aedes koreicus, an invasive mosquito rapidly expanding in several European countries, has shown competence for some arboviruses, but its role in dengue virus transmission remains unknown. This study aimed to assess, for the first time, the vector competence of an Italian population of Ae. koreicus for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1). Methods Laboratory-reared Ae. koreicus females originating from northeastern Italy were orally infected with DENV-1 via an artificial blood meal. Mosquitoes were maintained at 26 ± 1 °C and analysed at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-infection (dpi). Infection, dissemination and transmission were evaluated by RT-qPCR and droplet digital PCR, while the presence of infectious virus in saliva was confirmed by virus isolation in Vero E6 cells. Results Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. Viral dissemination to legs and wings was detected from 14 dpi onwards, reaching 100% at 21 and 28 dpi. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days post-infection (dpi), indicating a relatively long extrinsic incubation period. Overall transmission rate and efficiency were 33.3% and 20%, respectively, at later time points. Infectious virus was successfully isolated from saliva samples confirming transmission capability. Conclusions Aedes koreicus was shown to be susceptible to DENV-1 infection and capable of transmitting the virus, although with low efficiency and a long extrinsic incubation period. Despite these limitations, its increasing abundance, longevity and capacity to feed on humans suggest that it may act as a potential dengue vector under favourable conditions. These findings highlight the need to include Ae. koreicus in entomological surveillance and risk assessments for dengue transmission in Europe. analysis.research_question_and_background: The increasing incidence of dengue in Europe, combined with the spread of invasive mosquito species, raises concerns about the emergence of new vectors. This study aimed to assess, for the first time, the vector competence of an Italian population of Ae. koreicus for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Laboratory-reared Ae. koreicus females originating from northeastern Italy were orally infected with DENV-1 via an artificial blood meal. Mosquitoes were maintained at 26 ± 1 °C and analysed at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-infection (dpi).
analysis.methods: Infection, dissemination and transmission were evaluated by RT-qPCR and droplet digital PCR, while the presence of infectious virus in saliva was confirmed by virus isolation in Vero E6 cells.
analysis.main_results: Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. Viral dissemination to legs and wings was detected from 14 dpi onwards, reaching 100% at 21 and 28 dpi. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days post-infection (dpi), indicating a relatively long extrinsic incubation period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Aedes koreicus was shown to be susceptible to DENV-1 infection and capable of transmitting the virus, although with low efficiency and a long extrinsic incubation period. Despite these limitations, its increasing abundance, longevity and capacity to feed on humans suggest that it may act as a potential dengue vector under favourable conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the need to include Ae. koreicus in entomological surveillance and risk assessments for dengue transmission in Europe.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the laboratory-based nature of the study and the relatively low transmission efficiency observed. The study was conducted under controlled conditions, which may not fully reflect real-world transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the vector competence of Aedes koreicus, an invasive mosquito species in Italy, for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1). Laboratory-reared mosquitoes were orally infected with DENV-1 and analyzed at multiple time points. Results showed that Ae. koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60%, and viral dissemination reached 100% by 21 days post-infection. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days, confirming transmission capability, though with low efficiency (20%) and a long extrinsic incubation period. The findings suggest that Ae. koreicus could potentially act as a dengue vector under favorable conditions, highlighting the need for its inclusion in European entomological surveillance and risk assessments.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 实验室培养的 Ae。来自意大利东北部的雌性 koreicus 通过人工血粉经口感染 DENV-1。将蚊子维持在 26 ± 1 °C,并在感染后 7、14、21 和 28 天 (dpi) 进行分析。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 RT-qPCR 和液滴数字 PCR 评估感染、传播和 传播,同时通过 Vero E6 细胞中的病毒分离证实唾液中感染性病毒的存在。
elements_zh.main_results: Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 朝鲜伊蚊被证明对 DENV-1 感染敏感,并且能够传播病毒,但效率低且外源性潜伏期长。尽管存在这些限制,但其不断增加的丰度、寿命和以人类为食的能力表明,在有利的条件下,它可能充当潜在的登革热 媒介。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了将 Ae 纳入其中的必要性。koreicus 在欧洲昆虫学 监测 和登革热 传播 风险评估中的应用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于该研究基于实验室的性质以及观察到的 传播 效率相对较低,因此证据强度中等。该研究是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全反映现实世界的 传播 动态。

papers.title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
papers.abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

papers.title: De veranderende epidemiologie van vectorziekten
papers.abstract: Het augustusnummer van het Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg bevat een bijdrage over virusinfecties met “exotische” muggen in de rol van vector (1). Intuïtief maken wij dan de associatie met verre reizen. Maar, er is meer aan de hand. “Vector-borne diseases” of vectorziekten vertegenwoordigen 17% van alle infectieziekten wereldwijd en zijn verantwoordelijk voor meer dan 700.000 overlijdens per jaar (2, 3). Die vectoren zijn artropoden (zoals muggen en teken) die pathogene micro-organismen (virussen, parasieten of bacteriën) kunnen overdragen op een gastheer wanneer zij een bloedmaaltijd gebruiken (2). Het gaat over koortsige ziekten zoals bijvoorbeeld malaria, gele koorts, dengue, chikungunya en zika. Het risico om zo een infectie op te lopen, is het grootst in die delen van de wereld met een warm en vochtig klimaat (3). Maar, in de voorbije 2 decennia was er een merkelijke toename in incidentie en verdeling van sommige van deze ziekten in Europa (4, 5). Dat heeft deels te maken met de toenemende globalisering, meer intercontinentaal reisverkeer en handelstranport wereldwijd, wat de verspreiding van vectoren in de hand werkt (4, 6). Terugkerende reizigers kunnen inderdaad een door vectoren overgebrachte infectie oplopen als “importziekte” omdat zij tijdens hun verblijf in een endemische streek gestoken werden door exotische muggen. Maar toch wordt ook in Europa in toenemende mate “autochtone transmissie” van door muggen overdraagbare pathogenen beschreven (7). De transmissie gebeurt dan doordat een teruggekeerde reiziger met viremie in eigen land geprikt wordt door een mug die een geschikte vector is, daarbij het pathogene micro-organisme opneemt en het dan doorgeeft aan een nog niet geïnfecteerd iemand bij een volgende prik (6). Een essentiële voorwaarde voor dit mechanisme is uiteraard dat de vector zich in het nieuwe land gevestigd heeft en zich daar kan handhaven. Meer en meer wordt aangenomen dat de klimaatverandering in belangrijke mate dit process aandrijft (8, 9). Hogere temperaturen, andere neerslagpatronen en zachtere winters zouden de vestiging en verspreiding van vectorartropoden in voordien niet-endemische regio’s mogelijk maken. Het gaat dan vooral om muggen van het species Aedes, Anopheles en Culex, en “sandflies” van het species Phlebotomus (8). Het ectothermische karakter van deze artropoden, die de eigen lichaamstemperatuur niet kunnen reguleren, maakt hen zeer gevoelig aan externe klimaatomstandigheden. Daarnaast is de omgevingstemperatuur mee bepalend voor de maturatie en replicatie van de pathogenen die door die atropoden meegedragen worden (10, 11). Op dezelfde manier wordt overigens ook de natuurlijke epidemiologie beïnvloed van ziekten die reeds autochtoon waren in Europa, zoals leishmaniasis, met sandflies als vector, en infectie met West Nile-virus, met Culex-muggen als vector (8). Aedes albopictus of de Aziatische tijgermug, vector van arbovirussen zoals dengue en chikungunya, is een voorbeeld bij uitstek van een exotische muggensoort die zich gestaag blijft verspreiden over het Europese continent na daar voor het eerst verschenen te zijn in de late jaren 70. Zo werd de eerste autochtone uitbraak van chikungunya in Europa gedocumenteerd in Italië in 2007, en van dengue in Kroatië in 2010. Later volgden herhaalde uitbraken van deze ziekten in Italië, Frankrijk en Spanje (6, 12). België ligt op het pad van de verder noordwaartse verplaatsing van deze mug, die zich er in toenemende mate vestigt en ook overwintert. Dat is gebleken uit projecten van surveillance, zoals MEMO en MEMO+ (acroniem voor “Monitoring of Exotic Mosquitoes”) als onderdeel van het groter “National Environmental Health Action Plan” of NEHAP (13, 14, 15). Observaties in andere delen van de wereld hebben aangetoond dat plaatselijke uitbraken van virusziekte overgebracht door Aedes-muggen zich typisch voordeden met een interval van 5 tot 15 jaar nadat deze muggensoort zich gevestigd had (5, 16). Europese data lijken de mogelijkheid van een dergelijk patroon te ondersteunen, want zij tonen een sterke toename van autochtone gevallen van dengue in landen waar Aedes albopictus al sinds meerdere jaren gedijt (5). Deze bevindingen moeten ons er dus toe aanzetten om de kans op een ernstige infectieziekte overgebracht door muggen niet meer louter als een “ver-van-mijn-bedhypothese” weg te dringen wanneer in de anamnese een typische hint zoals “terugkeer van een verre reis” ontbreekt. Want hoewel nu misschien nog geen vaste prik in onze standaardlijst van differentiaaldiagnosen van een koortsige ziekte, kan de optie van een door muggen overdraagbare infectie in de toekomst mogelijk vaker het overwegen waard worden. Patrick Lacor, hoofdredacteur

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the changing epidemiology of vector-borne diseases, focusing on the emergence of exotic mosquito-borne infections in Europe and the role of climate change in facilitating their establishment and transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review article published in the Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg, discussing global and European epidemiological trends of vector-borne diseases without primary data collection.
analysis.methods: The review synthesizes existing literature and surveillance data on vector-borne diseases, including projects like MEMO and MEMO+, to analyze the spread of exotic mosquitoes and autochthonous transmission patterns in Europe.
analysis.main_results: Vector-borne diseases represent 17% of all infectious diseases globally, causing over 700,000 deaths annually; Europe has seen a marked increase in incidence and distribution of diseases like dengue and chikungunya, with autochthonous transmission documented in Italy, Croatia, France, and Spain.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret climate change as a key driver for the establishment of exotic vectors like Aedes albopictus in Europe, noting a pattern of local outbreaks occurring 5-15 years after vector introduction, challenging the perception of mosquito-borne infections as solely 'imported' diseases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings underscore the need to revise differential diagnoses for febrile illnesses to include locally transmitted mosquito-borne infections and enhance surveillance systems to anticipate future outbreaks in non-endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on observational data and literature review, limiting causal inference; however, the consistency of global and European data supports a moderate assessment of the reported trends.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the changing epidemiology of vector-borne diseases, particularly the emergence of exotic mosquito-borne infections in Europe. It highlights that vector-borne diseases constitute 17% of global infectious diseases, causing over 700,000 deaths annually. The study attributes the rise in autochthonous transmission of diseases like dengue and chikungunya in Europe to climate change, globalization, and the establishment of exotic vectors such as Aedes albopictus. Surveillance projects like MEMO and MEMO+ document the northward spread of these vectors, with outbreaks occurring 5-15 years after their introduction. The authors emphasize the need to reconsider differential diagnoses for febrile illnesses, as locally transmitted mosquito-borne infections may become more common in previously non-endemic regions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了 媒介 传播疾病的 媒介 变化,重点关注欧洲外来蚊媒感染的出现以及气候变化在促进其传播和 媒介 传播疾病中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是发表在 Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg 上的叙述性评论文章,讨论了在没有原始数据收集的情况下 媒介 传播疾病的全球和欧洲流行病学趋势。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述综合了有关 媒介 传播疾病的现有文献和 监测 数据,包括 MEMO 和 MEMO+ 等项目,以分析外来蚊子和本土 传播 模式在欧洲的传播。
elements_zh.main_results: Vector-borne diseases represent 17% of all infectious diseases globally, causing over 700,000 deaths annually; Europe has seen a marked increase in incidence and distribution of diseases like dengue and chikungunya, with autochthonous transmission documented in Italy, Croatia, France, and Spain.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将气候变化解释为白纹伊蚊等外来 媒介 在欧洲建立的关键驱动因素,并指出 媒介 引入后 5-15 年出现当地 媒介 的模式,挑战了蚊媒感染仅作为“输入”疾病的看法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要修改发热性疾病的鉴别诊断,将本地传播的蚊媒感染纳入其中,并增强 监测 系统以预测非流行地区未来的 监测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于观察数据和文献综述,限制因果推断;然而,全球和欧洲数据的一致性支持对报告趋势进行适度评估。

papers.title: Sequence Homology and Tissue Tropism Determine Superinfection Exclusion of Zika virus in Aedes aegypti Mediated by an insect-specific Binjari-Zika Virus Chimera
papers.abstract: Arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses cause widespread disease and continue to expand their geographical range due to climate change and vector spread. Insect-specific flaviviruses (ISFs) are promising biocontrol candidates of arboviruses, due to recent studies showing that prior infection with an ISF can reduce arbovirus replication in mosquitoes through superinfection exclusion (SIE). However, the route of infection, tissue tropism, pathogenesis and the mechanisms underlying SIE of ISFs in mosquitoes remain unclear. RNA interference (RNAi) is a potent antiviral response in insects, therefore it is expected that sequence homology between the ISF and the arbovirus will strengthen SIE. Here, we used ISF Binjari virus and a chimera containing the Zika virus structural proteins prME (BinJ-ZIKV) as a model system. Intrathoracic injection of BinJ-ZIKV in Aedes aegypti led to rapid systemic infection that excluded the midgut, subsequently blocking ZIKV dissemination from the midgut. SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest. This spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus and displayed a strong 21nt siRNA response, suggesting RNAi contributed to the observed SIE. Upon oral inoculation, BinJ-ZIKV replicated efficiently in mosquitoes, was detected across multiple tissues, and saliva. BinJ-ZIKV also had higher infection establishment than BinJV at lower oral titres. SIE was observed for BinJ-ZIKV infection after oral exposure interfered with subsequent ZIKV midgut infection. Together, these findings support engineered ISF-chimeras as valuable experimental tools to dissect viral determinants of SIE and to optimize mosquito-based arbovirus interference strategies.

Dengue viruses, which cause widespread disease, are of significant public health concern due to their expanding geographical range.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a model system involving the insect-specific Binjari virus and a Binjari-Zika virus chimera (BinJ-ZIKV) in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. analysis.methods: The researchers employed RNA interference (RNAi) as a mechanism to analyze the antiviral response in mosquitoes. They injected BinJ-ZIKV intrathoracically and orally inoculated it to assess its impact on ZIKV dissemination and replication.
analysis.main_results: Intrathoracic injection of BinJ-ZIKV led to rapid systemic infection that excluded the midgut, thereby blocking ZIKV dissemination. SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest, and the spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that sequence homology and tissue tropism are critical factors in determining SIE, with RNAi playing a significant role. papers.title: Molecular analysis and computational modeling reveal temporally separable responses triggered by DENV-induced soluble factors in endothelial cells
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) represents a growing global health challenge with billions of people at risk. Severe Dengue (SD), a complication of DENV infection that involves generalized hemorrhage, is driven, at least in part, by endothelial dysfunction. Endothelial dysfunction refers to increased permeability due to inflammation, mechanical injury and/or modification of the genetic program of endothelial cells. Previous work showed that exposure of endothelial cells to conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV) increased permeability and cellular stiffness, repressed endothelial markers and induced mesenchymal genes. However, the generality, extent, mechanism and ultimate impact of these events in the onset of SD remain elusive. Here, we integrate analysis from in vitro treatment of endothelial cells with media containing UV-inactivated DENV with computational modeling to investigate the key features of CMDV-induced endothelial alterations and their potential impact on endothelial dysfunction. We found that CMDV increased SNA1 and CDH2 expression, while suppressing endothelial genes OCLN and CDH5 . Global transcriptomics analysis revealed that CMDV triggered a transient pro-inflammatory response, followed by induction of selected tissue repair genes and matrix remodeling. A non-directed asynchronous network model (NDAM-CMDV) identified IL6 and FN1 as central nodes of DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation, providing new molecular insights that predict the evolution of the disease and identify potential therapeutic targets.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) poses a major global health burden with severe dengue (SD) driven by endothelial dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking DENV-induced soluble factors to endothelial alterations and SD onset remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used in vitro treatment of endothelial cells with conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV) and integrated transcriptomics with computational modeling to investigate endothelial responses.
analysis.methods: Endothelial cells were exposed to CMDV, and global transcriptomic profiling was performed to assess gene expression changes, followed by construction of a non-directed asynchronous network model (NDAM-CMDV) to identify central regulatory nodes.
analysis.main_results: CMDV exposure increased SNA1 and CDH2 expression while suppressing endothelial genes OCLN and CDH5, and triggered a transient pro-inflammatory response followed by induction of tissue repair and matrix remodeling genes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that DENV-induced soluble factors drive endothelial trans-differentiation, with IL6 and FN1 identified as central nodes in a network model that predicts disease evolution and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that targeting IL6 and FN1 pathways may mitigate endothelial dysfunction in dengue, informing future therapeutic strategies and surveillance approaches for severe dengue.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro models and computational predictions, lacking in vivo validation or clinical correlation, warranting cautious interpretation and further experimental confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how soluble factors from DENV-infected cells alter endothelial cell function, a process implicated in severe dengue pathogenesis. Using in vitro exposure of endothelial cells to conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV), the authors observed increased expression of mesenchymal markers (SNA1, CDH2) and suppression of endothelial markers (OCLN, CDH5), alongside a transient pro-inflammatory response followed by tissue repair and matrix remodeling gene induction. Computational modeling identified IL6 and FN1 as central regulatory nodes in DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation, proposing these as potential therapeutic targets. While the findings provide mechanistic insights into endothelial dysfunction during dengue infection, the study is limited to in vitro and computational analyses without in vivo validation, constraining the strength of evidence and generalizability.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 重症登革热 (DENV) 与由内皮功能障碍驱动的 重症登革热 (SD) 构成了重大的全球健康负担,但将 DENV 诱导的可溶性因子与内皮改变和 SD 发病联系起来的机制仍知之甚少。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用内皮细胞的体外 治疗 和来自 DENV 感染细胞 (CMDV) 的条件培养基,并将转录组学与计算模型相结合来研究内皮反应。
analysis_zh.methods: 将内皮细胞暴露于 CMDV,并进行全局转录组分析以评估基因表达变化,然后构建非定向异步网络模型 (NDAM-CMDV) 以识别中央调节节点。
analysis_zh.main_results: CMDV 暴露增加了 SN​​A1 和 CDH2 的表达,同时抑制内皮基因 OCLN 和 CDH5,并引发短暂的促炎症反应,随后诱导组织修复和基质重塑基因。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为 DENV 诱导的可溶性因子驱动内皮转分化的证据,其中 IL6 和 FN1 被确定为预测疾病 进化 和潜在治疗靶点的网络模型中的中心节点。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究表明,靶向 IL6 和 FN1 通路可能会减轻登革热的内皮功能障碍,为未来的治疗策略和 重症登革热 的 监测 方法提供信息。

papers.title: Virus-specific alterations in placental structure and transporter expression following maternal arbovirus infection.
papers.abstract: We hypothesized that arboviruses impair the placental expression of key functional markers implicated in fetal brain development. Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed. Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken. Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Histopathology detected predominantly mild vascular and stromal lesions across groups, with DENV placentae exhibiting moderate congestion in 100% of cases. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. MCT8 expression was significantly elevated in CHIKV. Placental Ki-67 was increased in CHIKV/ZIKV, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced and p-mTOR signalling was increased across all arbovirus-exposed placentae, while MMP9 expression was unchanged. Principal components analysis (PCA) distinguished infected from uninfected groups based on placental functional markers related to fetal brain development, but not on histomorphometry. Arboviral-infected placentae showed distinct structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability and long-term neurodevelopmental risks, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. KEY POINTS: Virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas. Arboviruses reduced the placental efflux transporters P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and disrupted the expression of ABCA1, SNAT2, GLUT1 and SNAT4 nutrient transporters, while ZIKV additionally reduced SNAT1 expression. Placental functional adaptation to arboviral infection comprised changes in the expression of placental markers of proliferation (Ki-67), angiogenesis (VEGFB), and nutrient sensing (p-mTOR). Arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibited greater functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of major neonatal abnormalities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether maternal arbovirus infection, including dengue virus (DENV), alters placental structure and transporter expression relevant to fetal brain development, motivated by gaps in understanding virus-specific placental pathology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Singleton placentae (n = 54) from pregnancies affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed.
analysis.methods: Immunohistochemical quantification of transporter systems, cell turnover markers, signalling pathways, and histomorphometric features related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was performed.
analysis.main_results: Birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC, and DENV placentae showed increased fetal blood vessel area and reduced connective tissue area; decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 was detected in all groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibit virus-specific structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment even without neonatal symptoms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that DENV infection may contribute to placental changes that could influence fetal growth and long-term neurodevelopmental risk, informing surveillance and research priorities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size, cross-sectional design, and lack of mechanistic or longitudinal neurodevelopmental follow-up, warranting cautious interpretation and further research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether maternal arbovirus infection, including dengue virus (DENV), alters placental structure and transporter expression relevant to fetal brain development. Singleton placentae from pregnancies affected by chikungunya (CHIKV), dengue (DENV), zika (ZIKV), or healthy controls were analysed using immunohistochemistry and histomorphometry. DENV-exposed placentae showed increased fetal blood vessel area and reduced connective tissue area, alongside decreased expression of placental transporters (P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1, SNAT2) across all groups. Birth weight was lower in DENV pregnancies compared with controls. The authors concluded that arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibit virus-specific structural and functional alterations, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. These findings suggest possible subclinical impacts on fetal growth and neurodevelopment, highlighting the need for surveillance and further mechanistic studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了母体虫媒病毒感染,包括 登革病毒 (DENV),是否会改变与胎儿大脑发育相关的胎盘结构和转运蛋白表达,其动机是对病毒特异性胎盘病理学的理解存在差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对受基孔肯雅热(CHIKV,n = 12)、登革热(DENV,n = 8)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV,n = 15)或健康对照(HC,n = 15)影响的妊娠的单胎胎盘(n = 54)进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 对转运系统、细胞周转标记物、信号通路以及与细胞外基质重塑、血管维护和营养传感相关的组织形态学特征进行免疫组织化学定量。
elements_zh.main_results: 与HC相比,DENV妊娠的出生体重降低,且DENV胎盘表现出胎儿血管面积增加和结缔组织面积减少;所有组中均检测到 P-gp、BCRP、ABCA1 和 SNAT2 表达下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,暴露于虫媒病毒的胎盘表现出病毒特异性的结构重塑和转运蛋白表达的改变,这表明即使没有新生儿症状,也可能对胎儿神经发育产生潜在的亚临床影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,DENV 感染可能会导致胎盘变化,从而影响胎儿生长和长期神经发育风险,为 监测 和研究重点提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小、横截面设计以及缺乏机制或纵向神经发育随访的限制,需要谨慎解释和进一步研究。

papers.title_zh: 母体虫媒病毒感染后胎盘结构和转运蛋白表达的病毒特异性改变。
papers.source_body_en: We hypothesized that arboviruses impair the placental expression of key functional markers implicated in fetal brain development. Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed. Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken. Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Histopathology detected predominantly mild vascular and stromal lesions across groups, with DENV placentae exhibiting moderate congestion in 100% of cases. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. MCT8 expression was significantly elevated in CHIKV. Placental Ki-67 was increased in CHIKV/ZIKV, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced and p-mTOR signalling was increased across all arbovirus-exposed placentae, while MMP9 expression was unchanged. Principal components analysis (PCA) distinguished infected from uninfected groups based on placental functional markers related to fetal brain development, but not on histomorphometry. Arboviral-infected placentae showed distinct structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability and long-term neurodevelopmental risks, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. KEY POINTS: Virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas. Arboviruses reduced the placental efflux transporters P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and disrupted the expression of ABCA1, SNAT2, GLUT1 and SNAT4 nutrient transporters, while ZIKV additionally reduced SNAT1 expression. Placental functional adaptation to arboviral infection comprised changes in the expression of placental markers of proliferation (Ki-67), angiogenesis (VEGFB), and nutrient sensing (p-mTOR). Arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibited greater functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of major neonatal abnormalities.

papers.title: Equi-depth pooling for standardized and cost-effective Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire sequencing (AIRRseq)
papers.abstract: Bulk B- and T-cell adaptive immune receptor (BCR/TCR) repertoire sequencing (AIRRseq) enables comprehensive analysis of adaptive immune diversity, but achieving balanced sequencing depth across heterogeneous clinical samples remains a major cost driver. Standard equimolar pooling prior to sequencing disproportionately allocates reads, leading to undersequencing of libraries with high sequence abundance and oversampling of those with few sequences. Here, a quantitative pooling strategy is described in which libraries are pooled based on estimated target-specific unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts rather than library molarity, ensuring a uniform number of supporting reads per target sequence UMI across samples. Libraries were prepared from human RNA using the NEBNext Immune Sequencing (IS) kit and quantified by qPCR during the second amplification (PCR2) step. Deeply sequenced samples from a dengue 1 human infection model (DHIM1) clinical study were used to model the log-linear relationship between PCR2 cycle threshold (Ct) values and detected sequence counts. This model was then applied to a second, independent batch of samples from a dengue 3 human infection model (DHIM3) clinical study to predict UMI abundance and guide equi-depth pooling prior to sequencing. Sequencing of these equi-depth pools demonstrated a near-uniform reads-per-sequence ratio across samples, confirming that this approach achieves balanced depth without oversampling and at reduced cost. Simulations across a range of between-sample UMI-count distributions reflecting real-world sample pools showed that equi-depth pooling is expected to reduce the total number of required sequencing reads by approximately 70% compared with equimolar pooling, with savings increasing as the spread of library sizes grows. Beyond cost efficiency, equi-depth pooling eliminates the complexity-dependent sampling bias inherent to equimolar pooling, ensuring uniform sequencing depth and comparable UMI recovery across small and large libraries. For new workflows or sample types, implementation requires either an existing calibration dataset or a pilot sequencing experiment to establish the relationship between PCR2 Ct values and relative UMI abundance. The equi-depth method thus provides a robust, scalable, and cost-efficient strategy for bulk AIRRseq studies where library sizes vary widely.

papers.title_zh: 用于标准化且经济高效的自适应免疫受体库测序 (AIRRseq) 的等深度池化
papers.source_body_en: Bulk B- and T-cell adaptive immune receptor (BCR/TCR) repertoire sequencing (AIRRseq) enables comprehensive analysis of adaptive immune diversity, but achieving balanced sequencing depth across heterogeneous clinical samples remains a major cost driver. Standard equimolar pooling prior to sequencing disproportionately allocates reads, leading to undersequencing of libraries with high sequence abundance and oversampling of those with few sequences. Here, a quantitative pooling strategy is described in which libraries are pooled based on estimated target-specific unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts rather than library molarity, ensuring a uniform number of supporting reads per target sequence UMI across samples. Libraries were prepared from human RNA using the NEBNext Immune Sequencing (IS) kit and quantified by qPCR during the second amplification (PCR2) step. Deeply sequenced samples from a dengue 1 human infection model (DHIM1) clinical study were used to model the log-linear relationship between PCR2 cycle threshold (Ct) values and detected sequence counts. This model was then applied to a second, independent batch of samples from a dengue 3 human infection model (DHIM3) clinical study to predict UMI abundance and guide equi-depth pooling prior to sequencing. Sequencing of these equi-depth pools demonstrated a near-uniform reads-per-sequence ratio across samples, confirming that this approach achieves balanced depth without oversampling and at reduced cost. Simulations across a range of between-sample UMI-count distributions reflecting real-world sample pools showed that equi-depth pooling is expected to reduce the total number of required sequencing reads by approximately 70% compared with equimolar pooling, with savings increasing as the spread of library sizes grows. Beyond cost efficiency, equi-depth pooling eliminates the complexity-dependent sampling bias inherent to equimolar pooling, ensuring uniform sequencing depth and comparable UMI recovery across small and large libraries. For new workflows or sample types, implementation requires either an existing calibration dataset or a pilot sequencing experiment to establish the relationship between PCR2 Ct values and relative UMI abundance. The equi-depth method thus provides a robust, scalable, and cost-efficient strategy for bulk AIRRseq studies where library sizes vary widely.
papers.abstract_zh: 批量 B 和 T 细胞适应性免疫受体 (BCR/TCR) 全谱测序 (AIRRseq) 能够全面分析适应性免疫多样性,但在异质临床样本中实现平衡的测序深度仍然是主要的成本驱动因素。测序前的标准等摩尔合并会不成比例地分配读数,导致序列丰度较高的文库测序不足,而序列较少的文库则会过采样。这里描述了一种定量合并策略,其中基于估计的目标特异性唯一分子标识符 (UMI) 计数而不是文库摩尔浓度来合并文库,确保跨样本的每个目标序列 UMI 的支持读取数量一致。使用 NEBNext 免疫测序 (IS) 试剂盒从人类 RNA 中制备文库,并在第二个扩增 (PCR2) 步骤中通过 qPCR 进行定量。使用来自登革热 1 人类感染模型 (DHIM1) 临床研究的深度测序样本来模拟 PCR2 循环阈值 (Ct) 值和检测到的序列计数之间的对数线性关系。然后将该模型应用于来自登革热 3 人类感染模型 (DHIM3) 临床研究的第二批独立样本,以预测 UMI 丰度并指导测序前的等深度合并。这些等深度池的测序证明了样本之间几乎均匀的每序列读取比率,证实了这种方法可以在不过度采样的情况下以降低的成本实现平衡的深度。对反映真实世界样本池的一系列样本间 UMI 计数分布进行的模拟表明,与等摩尔池相比,等深度池预计可将所需测序读取总数减少约 70%,并且随着文库大小分布的扩大,节省量也会增加。除了成本效率之外,等深度合并还消除了等摩尔合并固有的复杂性相关采样偏差,确保了小型和大型文库的统一测序深度和可比较的 UMI 回收率。对于新的工作流程或样本类型,实施需要现有的校准数据集或试点测序实验来建立 PCR2 Ct 值和相对 UMI 丰度之间的关系。因此,等深度方法为文库大小差异很大的批量 AIRRseq 研究提供了一种稳健、可扩展且经济高效的策略。

papers.title: Interactions Between Inbreeding, Fitness and the Bacterial Microbiome in Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Laboratory and field populations of insects can experience a decline in fitness and loss of genetic diversity due to inbreeding depression and genetic drift, respectively. Matings among related individuals and small population size may also influence insect host microbiomes with consequences for fitness. In the dengue vector mosquito, Aedes aegypti , the bacterial microbiome is largely environmentally determined, but recent studies have also revealed host genetic components. We generated a panel of 55 inbred lines from either of two founding outbred populations of Ae. aegypti to test for associations between life history traits, inbreeding, allelic diversity, and microbiome composition using ddRADseq and bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequencing on pools of mosquitoes. Effects of inbreeding were diverse, with severe composite fitness costs in many lines but minimal costs in others despite similar low levels of genetic diversity. We found no strong relationship between major life history traits across inbred lines, suggesting that any costs due to inbreeding were trait specific. Bacterial microbiome analysis of pooled samples from a subset of lines revealed common microbes across lines, with Elizabethkingia , Aeromonas , and Ralstonia being the most abundant. Despite bacterial composition varying widely, there was no clear relationship between microbiome composition and fitness or population origin. However, there were several significant positive correlations between the relative abundance of different microbial taxa across lines. Our results demonstrate diverse impacts of inbreeding on the fitness of mosquito populations but with limited impacts on the microbiome.

elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform understanding of how inbreeding affects mosquito fitness and microbiome composition, which is relevant for vector control strategies and managing dengue virus transmission by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.

papers.title_zh: 埃及伊蚊近亲繁殖、适应性和细菌微生物组之间的相互作用。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Laboratory and field populations of insects can experience a decline in fitness and loss of genetic diversity due to inbreeding depression and genetic drift, respectively. Matings among related individuals and small population size may also influence insect host microbiomes with consequences for fitness. In the dengue vector mosquito, Aedes aegypti , the bacterial microbiome is largely environmentally determined, but recent studies have also revealed host genetic components. We generated a panel of 55 inbred lines from either of two founding outbred populations of Ae. aegypti to test for associations between life history traits, inbreeding, allelic diversity, and microbiome composition using ddRADseq and bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequencing on pools of mosquitoes. Effects of inbreeding were diverse, with severe composite fitness costs in many lines but minimal costs in others despite similar low levels of genetic diversity. We found no strong relationship between major life history traits across inbred lines, suggesting that any costs due to inbreeding were trait specific. Bacterial microbiome analysis of pooled samples from a subset of lines revealed common microbes across lines, with Elizabethkingia , Aeromonas , and Ralstonia being the most abundant. Despite bacterial composition varying widely, there was no clear relationship between microbiome composition and fitness or population origin. However, there were several significant positive correlations between the relative abundance of different microbial taxa across lines. Our results demonstrate diverse impacts of inbreeding on the fitness of mosquito populations but with limited impacts on the microbiome.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 实验室和野外昆虫种群可能分别由于近交衰退和遗传漂变而经历适应性下降和遗传多样性丧失。相关个体之间的交配和小种群规模也可能影响昆虫 宿主 微生物组,从而对健康产生影响。在登革热 媒介 蚊子(埃及伊蚊)中,细菌微生物组很大程度上是由环境决定的,但最近的研究也揭示了 宿主 的遗传成分。我们从伊蚊的两个创始远交种群中生成了一组 55 个近交系。埃及伊蚊使用 ddRADseq 和细菌 16S rRNA 基因测序对蚊子池测试生活史特征、近交、等位基因多样性和微生物组组成之间的关联。近亲繁殖的影响是多种多样的,尽管遗传多样性水平相似,但许多品系的综合适应度成本很高,但其他品系的成本却很小。我们发现近交系的主要生活史性状之间没有很强的关系,这表明近交造成的任何成本都是性状特异性的。对来自部分品系子集的汇集样本进行的细菌微生物组分析揭示了跨品系的常见微生物,其中伊丽莎白金氏菌属、气单胞菌属和罗尔斯通氏菌属最丰富。尽管细菌组成差异很大,但微生物组组成与适应性或种群起源之间没有明确的关系。然而,不同品系微生物类群的相对丰度之间存在一些显着的正相关性。我们的结果表明,近亲繁殖对蚊子种群的适应性有多种影响,但对微生物组的影响有限。

news.content: A Commonwealth of Virginia WebsiteAn official website of the Commonwealth of Virginia Here's how you knowAn official websiteHere's how you know To ensure accurate screen reader translation, please ensure you have the proper language packs installed.English ▼ ኣማርኛ العربية الفصحى 简化字 正體字 Français हिंदी 한국어 Español Tagalog اردو Tiếng Việt Find a Commonwealth Resource Skip to content Clinicians Search for: × About How Do I A-Z Index Locations Data Clinicians Newsroom Contact Virginia Department of Health > Clinicians > Clinician Letters > VDH Identifies a Locally Acquired Case of Dengue Virus Infection in Northern Virginia Resident Clinicians Clinician Letters Clinician Letter Archive Healthcare Professional Newsletter Disease Reporting Standing Orders Emergency Declarations Email this page VDH Identifies a Locally Acquired Case of Dengue Virus Infection in Northern Virginia Resident VDH Identifies a Locally Acquired Case of Dengue Virus Infection in a Northern Virginia Resident August 4, 2026 Dear Colleague, In collaboration with the Fairfax County and Loudoun County Health Departments, the Virginia Department of Health (VDH) is investigating a confirmed case of dengue virus infection in a resident who did not have known travel outside of Virginia prior to illness onset. This is the first documented case of locally acquired dengue in Virginia. The patient is known to have been in close proximity to a recent internationally acquired case in a Virginian who was diagnosed a couple weeks prior. Dengue viruses are spread to people through the bites of infected Aedes species mosquitoes. Transmission of the virus likely occurred when a local mosquito bit the internationally acquired case while infectious and subsequently infected the second case. There is no evidence of continued transmission and no additional reports of locally acquired dengue cases at this time. The potential risk for acquiring dengue virus in Virginia remains low. VDH is working with local partners to monitor for any additional dengue cases and conduct surveillance of mosquitoes that can carry dengue viruses. Given this recent report of local transmission, providers should: Advise patients on strategies to prevent mosquito bites. This will not only reduce risk of dengue but also of mosquito-borne disease endemic to Virginia, such as West Nile Virus. Aedes mosquitoes, which can transmit dengue virus, breed in water-filled containers that may be as small as a bottle cap. Advise patients to “tip and toss” containers around their homes and businesses that may hold water. Obtain a travel history for all patients presenting with acute febrile illness. Consider dengue in patients presenting with fever who live in or recently traveled to areas with risk of dengue. Consider dengue in patients without travel history if presenting with an acute febrile illness and strongly suggestive symptoms, including eye pain, muscle pain, joint pain, and bone pain. Alert your local health department immediately if you suspect dengue illness in a patient who has no history of travel to areas with risk of dengue or other risk factors for dengue infection, such as receiving a blood or organ transplant. Obtain diagnostic testing in suspect cases of dengue virus infection. Review the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidance on dengue case management, including recommendations by patient groups. Dengue Overview Most dengue cases reported in the United States are related to international travel to areas with known risk of dengue. As the types of mosquitoes that can spread dengue viruses are common in many areas of the United States, limited, local transmission of dengue has been documented in the United States. Rarely, dengue is spread in laboratory or healthcare setting exposures through blood transfusions, organ transplants, or needlestick injuries. Dengue can range from asymptomatic infection or mild illness to severe disease. The typical incubation period is 5–7 days. The usual clinical presentation includes acute onset of fever accompanied by any of the following symptoms: severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, nausea and vomiting, arthralgia, and macular or maculopapular rash. Mild symptoms of dengue can be confused with other illnesses that cause fever. Symptoms of dengue typically last 2–7 days. Most people will recover after about a week. Approximately one in 20 infected people develop severe dengue, which is a medical emergency. Symptoms of dengue can become severe within a few hours. Severe dengue can result in shock, internal bleeding, and death. Warning signs that have been associated with an increased risk for progression to severe dengue include: Severe abdominal pain or tenderness Persistent vomiting (≥3 episodes in 1 hr. or ≥4 episodes in 6 hrs.) Clinical fluid accumulation (e.g., pleural effusion, ascites, or pericardial effusion) Mucosal bleeding Altered mental status Liver enlargement Progressive increase of the hematocrit (in at least 2 consecutive measurements taken 6 hours apart). Laboratory Testing Diagnostic test recommendations for dengue depend on the patient’s phase of illness. In the acute phase (0-7 days after symptom onset), diagnostic testing should include both a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT), such as RT-PCR, and an IgM antibody test. Dengue virus antigen testing for nonstructural protein 1 (NS1 antigen test) can also be used to confirm infection. In the convalescent phase (>7 days post-symptom onset), only IgM antibody testing is recommended. If the timing of symptom onset is not clear, both NAAT and IgM should be ordered. If you have additional questions about dengue, please contact vectorborne@vdh.virginia.gov. On behalf of the entire VDH team, thank you for your partnership, dedication and determination in keeping Virginians safe and healthy. Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 3 August 2026) Format Situation Report Sources SPC WHO Posted 3 Aug 2026 Originally published 3 Aug 2026 Attachments Download Report (PDF | 750.72 KB) HIGHLIGHTS • Since 1 January 2025, twelve dengue outbreaks have been reported across Pacific Island Countries and Areas (PICs). • During 2025, dengue outbreaks were reported in American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, Samoa, Tonga, and Tuvalu. A total of 21,258 confirmed cases and 21 deaths were recorded across the Pacific. Fatalities were reported in Fiji (n=8), Samoa (n=7), Tonga (n=3), Nauru (n=2), and Kiribati (n=1). • Between 1 January 2026 and 2 July 2026, a total of 4 478 dengue confirmed cases, 173 hospitalisations and 3 deaths have been reported across the Pacific. • The Pacific Syndromic Surveillance System (PSSS) has reported a total of 8 852 Dengue-like Illness (DLI) cases to date, a lower trend compared to the same period last year. • In 2026 dengue outbreaks were officially declared in New Caledonia, Tonga and Shefa province Vanuatu. • The most affected countries and areas in 2026 include: Cook Islands, French Polynesia, Samoa, and New Caledonia. These account for 94% of confirmed cases. • Dengue serotype-1 (DENV-1) and serotype-2 (DENV-2) are currently in circulation. • The Cook Islands officially declared the end of its dengue outbreak on 25 May 2026. • As of 3 August 2026: o The dengue outbreak remains ongoing in Shefa Province, Vanuatu, with dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1) continuing to circulate. o Low levels of transmission are observed in American Samoa, Kiribati, New Caledonia, Samoa, and Tonga. o Tonga has declared end of dengue outbreak Related Content Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 27 July 2026) Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 20 July 2026) Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 10 July 2026) Fiji + 16 more Dengue in the Pacific: Multicountry Situation (As of 02 July 2026)

news.content_title: India’s dengue burden: All 4 virus strains circulate together in several states, DENV 2 most widespread
news.content:
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has revealed that four dengue virus serotypes - 1,2,3,4 have been simultaneously circulating across India, a trend that may shape the country’s dengue preparedness strategies.

The study, conducted by the ICMR through its Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (VRDL) network, analysed 6,889 laboratory-confirmed dengue samples collected from 45 laboratories across 25 States and Union Territories (UTs) between May 2023 and May 2025. DENV-2 was the most frequently reported serotype nationwide, accounting for 51 per cent of tested cases. It was followed by DENV-3 (13 per cent), DENV-1 (7 per cent) and DENV-4 (1 per cent).

Researchers found that every state and UT included in the study had at least two dengue serotypes circulating, indicating that dengue has become increasingly hyperendemic across India. According to the study, India contributes to 34 per cent (33 million) of the global burden of symptomatic dengue infections. Approximately 8.9 to 12.6 million primary infections are estimated to occur annually in the country among people aged 5 to 45.

.India gets its first Dengue vaccine—QDENGA.

“Molecular surveillance of dengue serotypes at regular intervals is critical for understanding serotype transmission dynamics and their burden on public health,” the authors wrote. They felt that earlier studies, although valuable, “were confined to smaller geographies” and “were not representative of temporal patterns.” Hence, could not be used for planning national strategies.

“The enhanced testing capabilities at the site laboratories also establish a robust platform for responding to future dengue epidemics, which pose a significant healthcare burden due to climate change, spread of vector mosquitoes and rapid urbanisation.”

Another concerning factor was patients facing concurrent infections. The study noted that such people were more likely to face thrombocytopenia (extremely low platelet count), hemorrhagic manifestations, and severe joint issues.

In most cases, dengue infection causes high fever, headache, weakness and muscle pain, but in severe cases it can be life-threatening. It can potentially lead to organ failure or severe bleeding if left untreated for a long time.

analysis.brief_en: India is experiencing a hyperendemic dengue situation with all four virus strains (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4) circulating simultaneously across 25 states and union territories, according to a recent ICMR study. The study underscores the need for regular molecular surveillance and enhanced testing capabilities to combat future epidemics, exacerbated by climate change and urbanization. India has also introduced its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA.

How to stay safe A case of dengue fever has been reported in Palm Beach County. Here's what to know. Maya Washburn Palm Beach Post Updated Aug. 3, 2026, 6:23 p.m. ET A case of the mosquito-borne illness dengue fever has been confirmed in Palm Beach County. Dengue fever is transmitted through the bite of specific mosquito species, including those found in Florida. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, and muscle pain, and while debilitating, the illness is rarely fatal. Someone has recently contracted dengue fever in Palm Beach County. The Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach County sent an advisory about a confirmed case of the mosquito-borne illness on Aug. 3. Miami-Dade County reported a local case on the same day. “DOH-Palm Beach and Palm Beach County Mosquito Control are coordinating surveillance and prevention efforts,” reads the Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach County release. Dengue fever is a disease related to the viruses that cause West Nile virus and yellow fever. Several cases are reported in Florida each year from people traveling to areas that have the disease, which usually include the Caribbean, Central and South America and Asia, according to the Florida Department of Health. It is common in many countries around the world and almost half of the world’s population live in areas at risk of dengue, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control. Still, no countries are in the CDC’s “high transmission” category for dengue fever right now. No countries have had 10 or more cases reported among travelers in the last three months as of July 1. How is dengue fever transmitted? Dengue infection is acquired through the bite of a certain species of mosquito. These include Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Both types of mosquito live in Florida. What are the symptoms of dengue fever? Dengue fever can be painful and debilitating, but it is rarely fatal, according to the Florida Department of Health. Symptoms start between three and 14 days after an infected mosquito bite. They include a sudden onset of fever, severe headache, eye pain, muscle and joint pain and bleeding. Vomiting and diarrhea are also possible. Symptoms usually last four to seven days. A more severe form of dengue is dengue hemorrhagic fever. It is rare, but it can be fatal if not treated. There is no treatment for dengue fever, but symptoms and complications can be managed. How to avoid dengue fever? People can protect themselves from getting bitten by mosquitoes. They can apply insect repellent to exposed skin or clothing, treat clothing with products containing 0.5% permethrin, be careful not to leave out standing water (where mosquitoes breed) and keep screens on windows. news.content: The two-dose TAK-003 vaccine regimen provides sustained protection against dengue, a clinical trial conducted in multiple countries, including Sri Lanka, has found, it is learnt. These data, including an exploratory analysis of a booster dose, confirm the favourable benefit and risk profile of TAK-003 and its efficacy in preventing Virologically Confirmed Dengue (VCD), said Dr [...] Home Archive Feeds Contact Us Feeds Editorials Times Online News » Columns Editorial Sunday Times 2 Plus Sports » Business Times Magazine » » Arts Mirror TV Times Funday Times Obituary Education » Archive Feeds Contact Us Sunday, August 02, 2026 News Vaccine also tested in SL gives “sustained” protection against dengue View(s): 151 The two-dose TAK-003 vaccine regimen provides sustained protection against dengue, a clinical trial conducted in multiple countries, including Sri Lanka, has found, it is learnt. These data, including an exploratory analysis of a booster dose, confirm the favourable benefit and risk profile of TAK-003 and its efficacy in preventing Virologically Confirmed Dengue (VCD), said Dr Eduardo Bittencourt de Gomensoro, explaining that VCD is usually tested through PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction – a laboratory method used to rapidly copy and amplify tiny pieces of DNA). Assuring that Takeda Pharmaceuticals had met all conditions set by the WHO for a Phase 3 Clinical Trial for a dengue vaccine, he ticked them off as: The participant numbers being 28,000; conducting the trials in eight countries where all four dengue serotypes were circulating; and the study period being 41⁄2 years, later extended for another 21⁄2 years Evidence of protection in 8 days Giving a glimpse of the Real World Evidence (RWE) gathered from an “elegant” study among 4 to 60-year-olds in Dourados in Brazil in 2024-25 during a dengue outbreak, Dr Eduardo Bittencourt de Gomensoro says that just eight days after being vaccinated with TAK-003, there was protection even without the production of antibodies. Dr Eduardo Bittencourt de Gomensoro Dispelling the misconception that vaccination should not take place during an outbreak of disease, he cited the strong example of the COVID-19 pandemic. Vaccination, which took place when the pandemic was raging, helped reduce deaths and disease severity. Vaccination protects the majority, he added. The four serotypes of the mosquito-borne virus causing dengue fever are: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4. Research on the current situation reportedly indicates that Sri Lanka is facing a raging epidemic due to about 80% of infections being caused by DENV-2 and the balance by DENV-3. Sri Lanka was part of the ‘TIDES’ study (Tetravalent Immunisation against Dengue Efficacy Study or DEN-301) to evaluate the safety and long-term efficacy of the TAK-003 vaccine from September 2016 to June 2024. It was the largest pivotal Phase 3 Clinical Trial undertaken by Takeda Pharmaceuticals. The study, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, saw more than 20,000 children and adolescents in the 4-16 age-group in eight dengue-endemic areas, including Sri Lanka, taking part. This type of study is the gold standard in medical research, combining random group assignment, inactive dummy treatments and masked participants and staff to eliminate human bias, it is understood. The other countries which participated in the study were the Philippines and Thailand from Asia and Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Panama from Latin America. TAK-003 is a dengue vaccine that is based on a live-attenuated dengue serotype 2 virus, which provides the genetic “backbone” for all four dengue virus serotypes. It is designed to help protect against any of these serotypes, states a press release from Takeda Pharmaceuticals. A ‘live-attenuated dengue serotype 2 virus’ means one which provides the genetic framework to stimulate broad immune protection, engineered to trigger neutralising antibodies without causing severe disease, it is understood. The ‘TIDES’ study comprised: Part 1 – Evaluation of Vaccine Efficacy (VE) and safety through 12 months after the second dose. Part 2 – Continuation for an additional six months to complete the assessment of the secondary endpoints of VE by serotype, baseline sero-status and disease severity including VE against hospitalized dengue. Part 3 – Evaluation of VE and long-term safety by following participants for an additional 21⁄2 to 3 years as per WHO recommendations. Part 4 – Evaluation of efficacy and safety for 13 months following booster vaccination. Part 5 – Evaluation of long-term efficacy and safety for one year following the completion of Part 4. news.title_zh: 疫苗 也在 SL 中进行了测试,可提供“持续”的登革热保护 - 斯里兰卡《星期日泰晤士报》
news.source_body_en: A major Phase 3 clinical trial, including Sri Lanka, confirms the TAK-003 dengue vaccine provides sustained protection against all four virus serotypes. The study, spanning 4.5 years with over 28,000 participants, demonstrated efficacy as early as 8 days post-vaccination, even without antibody production. Sri Lanka, part of the 'TIDES' study, faces an epidemic dominated by DENV-2 and DENV-3. The vaccine, based on a live-attenuated serotype 2 backbone, meets all WHO trial criteria. Researchers emphasize vaccination during outbreaks, citing COVID-19 evidence of reduced severity and deaths. Booster dose analysis and long-term safety continue to be evaluated.
news.content_zh: 包括斯里兰卡在内的一项大型 3 期临床试验证实,TAK-003 登革热 疫苗 可针对所有四种病毒血清型提供持续保护。这项研究历时 4.5 年,有超过 28,000 名参与者参与,早在 疫苗接种 后 8 天就证明了疗效,即使没有产生抗体。作为“潮汐”研究的一部分,斯里兰卡面临着以 DENV-2 和 DENV-3 为主的流行病。疫苗 基于减毒活血清 2 型骨干,符合所有 WHO 试验标准。研究人员在 暴发 期间强调 疫苗接种,引用了 COVID-19 严重程度和死亡率降低的证据。加强剂量分析和长期安全性仍在评估中。

news.content: Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Local Weather U.S. & World The Scene Politics Investigations Newsletters Watch 24/7 Create profile / Log in Dashboard Email preferences Sign out Trending 🐶 Clear the Shelters 🦚 4 on Tour 🌡️ Forecast 🔍 4 More Context 👂 All Ears Find Help 📨 NBC4 Newsletters 📺 Watch 24/7 Our News Standards Expand Virginia Dengue in Virginia: State reports 1st locally acquired case of mosquito-borne virus By Sophia Barnes • Published 4 hours ago • Updated 4 hours ago BOOKMARKER NBC Universal, Inc. Dengue fever is a viral infection spread by mosquitoes. Here’s what you need to know. A Northern Virginia resident diagnosed with the dengue virus in the state’s first locally acquired case of the illness transmitted by mosquitoes, the Virginia Department of Health (VDH) said. Ad More Sports TBS Graduates Bangladesh Supplement Infograph Explainer Archive Gallery Long Read Interviews Offbeat Magazine Climate Change Health Cartoons বাংলা THURSDAY, AUGUST 06, 2026 DENV-3 dominates dengue infections this year as experts fear more severe complications Health Tawsia Tajmim 02 August, 2026, 10:05 am Last modified: 02 August, 2026, 10:09 am Related News Dengue admissions top 500 daily, hospitals ready to open dedicated wards Dengue: 2 more die, 423 hospitalised in 24hrs Dengue: 3 more die, 467 hospitalised in 24 hours Dengue claims 3 more lives, 534 hospitalised in 24 hrs Three die of dengue, 458 more hospitalised in 24hrs DENV-3 dominates dengue infections this year as experts fear more severe complications Doctors are also reporting a rise in cases of expanded dengue syndrome, alongside dengue shock syndrome and prolonged fever, highlighting the need for early diagnosis, close monitoring and stronger mosquito control Tawsia Tajmim 02 August, 2026, 10:05 am Last modified: 02 August, 2026, 10:09 am Photo: Mehedi Hasan The DENV-3 serotype has become the dominant strain driving dengue infections in Bangladesh this year, raising concerns among health experts that the shift could lead to more severe illness, particularly in people previously infected with a different dengue variant. Doctors are also reporting a rise in cases of expanded dengue syndrome, alongside dengue shock syndrome and prolonged fever, highlighting the need for early diagnosis, close monitoring and stronger mosquito control. According to the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR), 91.5% of dengue samples serotyped this year were identified as DENV-3, while the remaining 8.5% were DENV-2. No other serotypes have been detected so far in 2026. Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel The institute has conducted RT-PCR serotyping on 71 samples recently. IEDCR Director Dr Quazi Ahmed Zaki told The Business Standard that although the number of samples remains limited, DENV-3 has clearly become the predominant serotype, replacing DENV-2, which had dominated in recent years. He explained that severe complications, including dengue shock syndrome, are more common in secondary infections. "If someone who was previously infected with one dengue serotype later contracts another, the body's immune response can increase the risk of severe disease," he said, noting that children, older adults and immunocompromised people remain most vulnerable. Zaki stressed that mosquito control remains the most effective way to reduce infections and deaths, warning that rising infections are likely to result in more fatalities unless breeding sites are eliminated. Public health expert Dr M Mushtuq Husain said the return of DENV-3 could leave many Bangladeshis more susceptible because immunity developed against DENV-2 offers little protection against a different serotype. "For several years, DENV-2 circulated widely. If DENV-3 now becomes dominant, people previously infected with DENV-2 may become infected again and face a higher risk of severe complications," he said. Meanwhile, the Directorate General of Health Services reported three dengue deaths and 534 new hospital admissions in the 24 hours leading up to 8am yesterday. This year's death toll has reached 50, while confirmed cases have risen to 14,690. Doctors report more cases of expanded dengue syndrome Dr Shahnoor Sarmin, associate professor of medicine and in-charge of the dengue ward at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, said physicians are seeing more cases of expanded dengue syndrome this year. "Besides fever, some patients are developing myocarditis, which is inflammation of the heart muscle, and encephalitis, or inflammation of the brain. We are also seeing prolonged fever and dengue shock syndrome," she said. Sarmin noted that it remains unclear whether the increase in such complications is directly linked to the dominance of DENV-3 because routine treatment does not include serotyping every patient. She added that the standard treatment protocol remains unchanged regardless of serotype. The expert urged people to get tested as soon as fever develops, saying early diagnosis enables timely treatment and monitoring. According to Sarmin, dengue management rests on three pillars: adequate rest, electrolyte-rich fluids and regular clinical monitoring. Patients should drink oral rehydration saline or other electrolyte-containing fluids rather than plain water, while paracetamol and sponging can help reduce fever. She warned that the most dangerous period is often the 24-48 hours after fever subsides, known as the critical or leakage phase. Symptoms such as low blood pressure, severe abdominal pain, chest pain, cold extremities or fainting require immediate hospital care. Sarmin also cautioned against focusing solely on platelet counts, saying that changes in blood pressure and haematocrit are more reliable indicators of life-threatening complications. news.title_zh: Dengue in Virginia: State reports 1st locally acquired case of mosquito-borne virus - NBC4 Washington
news.source_body_en: Virginia health officials have confirmed the state's first locally acquired case of dengue virus, a mosquito-borne illness. The case marks a significant public health development, as dengue is not typically endemic in the region. State authorities are investigating the circumstances of the local transmission, though details on the patient's condition, potential exposures, or ongoing control measures remain unspecified. The report underscores the importance of mosquito prevention efforts in Virginia, particularly during warmer months when mosquito activity is highest. Health officials are expected to provide further guidance as the investigation progresses.

urge mosquito prevention Health officials confirmed a locally acquired dengue fever case in Palm Beach County, warning residents to eliminate standing water and avoid mosquito bites Prev Next Photo by: WPTV By: Joel Lopez Posted 8:47 PM, Aug 03, 2026 and last updated 9:09 PM, Aug 03, 2026 PALM BEACH COUNTY, Fla. — Palm Beach County health officials have confirmed a locally acquired case of dengue fever, prompting a mosquito-borne illness advisory and warnings from health experts for residents to take mosquito prevention seriously. WATCH BELOW: 'If it happens to bite someone, that someone will likely get the infection,' Dengue fever confirmed in Palm Beach County: What you need to know Unlike most dengue cases seen in South Florida, the patient did not travel outside the area before getting sick. "The importance of this announcement is that this is the first case that would happen in someone who has not left Palm Beach County," Dr. Kleper De Almeida, an infectious disease specialist working at several hospitals in Palm Beach County, including Good Samaritan Medical Center, said. 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Every year, Florida sees what doctors call "imported cases" of dengue, where travelers become infected overseas and return home carrying the virus. But local transmission means mosquitoes in Palm Beach County are now carrying dengue and spreading it to people in the area. "What this means is that there are mosquitoes floating around, flying around, carrying the dengue virus," De Almeida said. "If it happens to bite someone, that someone will likely get the infection." Palm Beach County Locally-acquired dengue fever case confirmed in Palm Beach County Samantha Roesler 1:06 PM, Aug 03, 2026 Palm Beach County Mosquito Control has already been dispatched in response to the confirmed case. Health experts say the situation will likely not turn into a massive outbreak, but they do expect additional infections. "Usually one of these, having one case is a signal that there are mosquitoes flying around with the dengue virus," De Almeida said. "If infected mosquitoes bite an uninfected person, there is a good chance that the person will catch the infection." "We'll probably see a few people, and there would not be a huge number, hopefully," De Almeida said. Symptoms and treatment Dengue symptoms can be intense and often begin with fever and severe pain. "The telltale symptom is severe body aches, body and joint aches accompanied by a fever," De Almeida said. "Everything hurts. The lower back hurts, the joints hurt." Some patients may also develop a rash. "There is a rash that comes and goes," De Almeida said. In more severe cases, bleeding complications can develop, including a rash on the skin that does not blanch. "There are unfortunately no direct treatment," De Almeida said. "One has to wait it out." Doctors recommend using acetaminophen, like Tylenol, to manage fever and pain instead of medications like ibuprofen or aspirin, which could worsen bleeding complications. "If using aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen or other anti-inflammatory medications, it might exacerbate these bleeding complications," De Almeida said. How to reduce mosquito breeding at home Mosquito experts say one of the best ways to stop the spread starts in your own backyard. Harold Fortes with Mosquito Shield of Palm Beach said standing water is the primary concern. "What we're gonna do is spray all the vegetation," he said. "You see these pots right here? They hold water. So, what mosquitoes does is they lay eggs in there." Fortes said standing water can produce mosquitoes in as little as eight days, with some species breeding in as few as four days. "It's rainy season, big time for them to reproduce," he said. Residents are being urged to clean gutters, remove yard debris, and empty trays underneath flower pots. Experts also said bromeliad plants should be rinsed regularly, because they naturally collect water that can allow larvae to grow. Broader mosquito-borne illness threat De Almeida said dengue is just one of several dangerous illnesses spread by mosquitoes in Florida. "There is West Nile that causes a brain infection. There is chikungunya that causes severe joint and muscle pains. We remember Zika that happened a number of years ago," De Almeida said. His message to Palm Beach County residents is simple: avoid mosquito bites whenever possible. "We need to be more conscious, more attentive to not being bitten by mosquitoes during the summertime in Florida, because we can be acquiring one of these infections," De Almeida said. But local transmission means mosquitoes in Palm Beach County are now carrying dengue and spreading it to people in the area. "What this means is that there are mosquitoes floating around, flying around, carrying the dengue virus," De Almeida said. "If it happens to bite someone, that someone will likely get the infection." Palm Beach County Locally-acquired dengue fever case confirmed in Palm Beach County Samantha Roesler 1:06 PM, Aug 03, 2026 Palm Beach County Mosquito Control has already been dispatched in response to the confirmed case. Health experts say the situation will likely not turn into a massive outbreak, but they do expect additional infections. "Usually one of these, having one case is a signal that there are mosquitoes flying around with the dengue virus," De Almeida said. "If infected mosquitoes bite an uninfected person, there is a good chance that the person will catch the infection." "We'll probably see a few people, and there would not be a huge number, hopefully," De Almeida said. Symptoms and treatment Dengue symptoms can be intense and often begin with fever and severe pain. "The telltale symptom is severe body aches, body and joint aches accompanied by a fever," De Almeida said. "Everything hurts. The lower back hurts, the joints hurt." Some patients may also develop a rash. "There is a rash that comes and goes," De Almeida said. In more severe cases, bleeding complications can develop, including a rash on the skin that does not blanch. "There are unfortunately no direct treatment," De Almeida said. "One has to wait it out." Doctors recommend using acetaminophen, like Tylenol, to manage fever and pain instead of medications like ibuprofen or aspirin, which could worsen bleeding complications. "If using aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen or other anti-inflammatory medications, it might exacerbate these bleeding complications," De Almeida said. How to reduce mosquito breeding at home Mosquito experts say one of the best ways to stop the spread starts in your own backyard. Harold Fortes with Mosquito Shield of Palm Beach said standing water is the primary concern. "What we're gonna do is spray all the vegetation," he said. "You see these pots right here? They hold water. So, what mosquitoes does is they lay eggs in there." Fortes said standing water can produce mosquitoes in as little as eight days, with some species breeding in as few as four days. "It's rainy season, big time for them to reproduce," he said. Residents are being urged to clean gutters, remove yard debris, and empty trays underneath flower pots. Experts also said bromeliad plants should be rinsed regularly, because they naturally collect water that can allow larvae to grow. Broader mosquito-borne illness threat De Almeida said dengue is just one of several dangerous illnesses spread by mosquitoes in Florida. "There is West Nile that causes a brain infection. There is chikungunya that causes severe joint and muscle pains. We remember Zika that happened a number of years ago," De Almeida said. His message to Palm Beach County residents is simple: avoid mosquito bites whenever possible. "We need to be more conscious, more attentive to not being bitten by mosquitoes during the summertime in Florida, because we can be acquiring one of these infections," De Almeida said. Advertisement Updated: 8:00 AM EDT Aug 4, 2026 Editorial Standards i Caleb Califano Reporter Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Updated: 8:00 AM EDT Aug 4, 2026 Editorial Standards i Caleb Califano Reporter WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — Palm Beach County has confirmed a locally acquired case of dengue fever, prompting mosquito control crews to ramp up surveillance and treatment efforts across the area. Dengue fever case confirmed in Palm Beach County For Palm Beach County Mosquito Control, preparing for cases like this is a year-round effort, and the team is working closely with the Florida Department of Health. Advertisement “They're out there to make more mosquitoes. And along with it, they make us sick. So that's what we're here to try and stop,” said Steven Fazekas of Palm Beach County Mosquito Control. Palm Beach County reports Florida's first 'flesh-eating bacteria' death this year Fazekas said that crews are increasing surveillance across different parts of the county, setting traps, and treating areas as needed. Collected samples are brought back to the lab for analysis. “If we get a trap collection, we will bring it in. We identify the species under the microscope. We get, on a given year, 30 or 40 different species of mosquitoes in our area. And like I said, the type of mosquito matters whether they can transmit the virus or not,” Fazekas said. Experts say dengue fever is more commonly seen in other parts of the world, but most U.S. cases occur in the Southeast. Symptoms include high fevers, severe headaches, muscle aches, and rashes. Severe cases, while rare, can be deadly. Man arrested after PIT maneuver in Martin County sends family’s car into barbed-wire fence Fazekas noted that dengue fever is caused by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which is common in South Florida. Unlike other mosquito species, Aedes aegypti can be active during the daytime and breeds quickly in standing water. “If it pools water for a week or more, you got a chance of them finding it and growing in that water,” Fazekas said. To reduce the risk of mosquitoes around homes, residents are advised to dump standing water from items like buckets, flower pots, and children’s toys, as well as use bug spray and wear protective clothing.
